summary: A one-time code, entered as one field behind a row of boxes.

pairs.dont: Build the row as one input per digit.
pairs.do: Keep the single field this component is built on.
pairs.why: Six inputs are six tab stops, six paste targets and a pile of focus-shuffling code — and screen readers announce six unlabelled boxes instead of one code.

pairs.dont: Block paste to keep the boxes tidy.
pairs.do: Accept a pasted code and spread it across the slots.
pairs.why: The code arrives in another app. Pasting is how almost everyone enters it, and blocking it makes people retype from memory.

pairs.dont: Turn the boxes red and stop there.
pairs.do: Say what went wrong and offer a resend.
pairs.why: A wrong code is usually an expired one. Without a resend the only option is to start the whole flow again.

pairs.dont: Ask for the code with no context.
pairs.why: People check the wrong device otherwise, and there is no way to tell a delayed code from one sent somewhere they cannot reach.
A one-time code is short-lived and is being copied from another screen. Masking it removes the only way to check it was typed correctly.

pairs.do: Use md below about 420 of column.
pairs.why: Six lg slots are 56 each with an 8 gap, so the row needs 376 before any page padding — measured at 376 against a 360 column. md is 48 and fits at 328. The slots do not shrink on purpose: a code you cannot read is worse than one you have to scroll to.

a11y: Active is a data state rather than :focus-visible, because the real focus lives on a single hidden input while the visible slot that should look active is a different element.
invalid sets aria-invalid on the input as well as the treatment, so the error reaches assistive technology and not only the eye.
A disabled field has no active slot at all — there is nothing to point at when nothing is editable.
The caret is aria-hidden. Position is conveyed by the input's own selection, not by the drawn bar.
